gi16_aid.topic: US military aid to Israel: the 2016 MOU, emergency aid since Oct 2023, shares of budget and GDP, and the fungibility test

claims.text: CRS: 2016 MOU signed 14 Sept 2016 for FY2019–2028, $38bn: $33bn FMF grants plus $5bn missile defence; both sides commit 'not to seek changes to the FMF levels for the duration of this understanding'; MOU runs through 30 Sept 2028
CRS: total US aid obligations to Israel 1946–2025 about $174bn current dollars; about $298bn in constant 2024 dollars for 1946–2024

CRS: the 2007 MOU allowed up to 26.3% of aid to be spent on Israeli-made equipment (offshore procurement); under the 2016 MOU OSP decreases slowly until FY2024 then phases out more sharply, 'ending entirely in FY2028'

CRS: since FY1991 Congress has required Israel's FMF to be disbursed as a lump sum in the first month of the fiscal year, into an interest-bearing account at the Federal Reserve Bank; annual FMF grants are 'approximately 14%' of Israel's overall defence budget; Israel's defence spending 8.8% of GDP in 2024

CRS on P.L. 118-50 (April 2024): FMF $3.5bn (of which $769.3m or more may be spent on Israeli equipment), missile defence $4bn, Iron Beam $1.2bn; two US-owned Iron Dome batteries transferred 24 Oct 2023; Aug 2024 notifications >$20bn incl. F-15IA $18.82bn; Jan 2025 Trump released hold on 1,800 MK-84 bombs; 28 Feb 2025 emergency declaration ~$4bn; Rubio said it 'reverse[d] the Biden Administration's partial arms embargo'; Israel's Defence Ministry (27 May 2025): more than 90,000 tons of armaments on 800 planes and 140 ships

INSS (Feb 2026): US military aid has fallen to 'about half a percent' of Israeli GDP and is 'roughly 15%' of Israel's defence budget; the option to convert aid to shekels for domestic procurement has been eroded and will disappear by 2028, so aid goes almost exclusively to procurement in the US; recommends a gradual move to a business partnership, not dollar-for-dollar replacement

Bandow (Cato, 2012) citing Israeli economist Gazit: in 2011 US aid was 1.5% of Israel's GDP, 4% of the government budget and 24% of security outlays; three-quarters of the $3bn had to buy US weapons, a hidden cost Gazit put at about $600m, 'a fifth of the nominal' aid; Bandow: 'money is fungible' (applied to Egypt and Jordan aid)

National Interest (June 2016): 'Money is fungible'; OSP of $815m, just over 26% of the package, lets Israel 'divert funds from its defense-technology accounts' to settlements; estimated settlement spending at least $250m a year (uncertain, spread across accounts); proposed withholding OSP tied to settlement spending

Loan guarantees (CRS data via JVL): the 1992 $10bn guarantees (P.L. 102-391) could be reduced by an amount equal to Israel's settlement expenditures; reductions 1994–97 totalled $1,358.8m, less $585m reinstated for security, net $773.8m; under the 2003 $9bn guarantees reductions of $289.5m (2003) and $795.8m (2005)

Bank of Israel: defence expenditure 5.3% of GDP (2015–19 avg), 4.2% (2022), 5.2% (2023), 8.4% (2024), 7.8% (2025), ~5.5% projected 2026–30; gross war cost NIS 34bn (2023), 133bn (2024), 116bn (2025), 69bn projected (2026), total NIS 352bn ('approximately NIS 350 billion'), excluding decisions after late Feb 2026; special US grant NIS 13bn (2023), 6bn (2024), 6bn (2025), total NIS 25bn; gross public debt 61.3% (2023), 67.6% (2024), 68.5% (2025) of GDP

Knesset passed the 2026 budget 30 March 2026, 62-55; defence budget about $44.8bn, about $9.48bn more than previous year; record $268bn total; Bismuth: 'approximately ₪22 billion' of it is 'expenditure contingent on income, including the U.S. aid grant and other revenues'

Next MOU: Axios (Nov 2025) reported Israel sought a 20-year deal shifting toward joint R&D; Netanyahu (Jan 2026) called for winding down aid over a decade; in a 1 June 2026 letter to Rep. Stutzman: 'The time has now arrived for us to move from aid recipient to partner'; Huckabee: 'New MOU w/ Israel ends aid & will be based on trade'; joint statement aim 'gradually transition from aid to a completely reciprocal partnership'; formal talks began week of 1 June 2026

Netanyahu, CNBC interview (June 2026): 'I want it to start now, I want it to start in the last two years of the Trump administration', until aid reaches 'coming to zero'; Trump was initially not supportive when Netanyahu raised it in late December
